newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian average lending rate rises 110 bps to 12..
newsitem.headline: Croatian average lending rate rises 110 bps to 12..

text.p: The Croatian average money market rate climbed to 12.2 percent on Monday from 11.1 percent on a tight market.
Daily trade totalled 70.1 million kuna, leaving a shortage of 20.9 million in demand. Dealers said tight accounts made it difficult to find funds for banks with shortages.

Fresh loans accounted for 50 million kuna of the total, most of which was call money granted at higher rates, mixed at 10.5, 11 and 14 percent. The weighted call money rate rose to 11 percent from 10.6 percent.
Smaller ammounts in three- and four-day term deals were struck at 10.5 percent and seven-day at 11 percent.
Insurers rolled over previous loans at 13 and 13.5 percent, up from nine percent.
Banks charged 15 and 16 percent for one-month old funds and 17 percent for two-week loans.
The central banks's kuna midrates eased to 6.1804 from 6.1685 versus the dollar and to firmed to 3.5795 from 3.5801 against the German mark. -- Laura Lui, 385-1-4557075
